:::{#exm-chance-agreement}
#### Chance agreement for the COVID-19 test

Apply the COVID-19 test of @exm-sensitivity and @exm-specificity
to the [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population) of @exm-prevalence,
with the test as the agent ($A = +$) and the disease status as the reference ($R = D$).
By @thm-prob-positive,
with [sensitivity](#def-sensitivity) $\text{sens} = 0.99$,
[specificity](#def-specificity) $\text{spec} = 0.99$,
and [prevalence](#def-prevalence) $\prev = \Prf{D} = 0.07$,
the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) of a positive test is:

$$
\ba
\Prf{+}
&= \text{sens} \cd \prev + \paren{1 - \text{spec}} \cd \paren{1 - \prev}
&& \text{(probability of a positive test)} \\
&= 0.99 \cd 0.07 + \paren{1 - 0.99} \cd \paren{1 - 0.07}
&& \text{(substitute the given values)} \\
&= 0.99 \cd 0.07 + 0.01 \cd 0.93
&& \text{(subtract inside each pair of parentheses)} \\
&= 0.0693 + 0.0093
&& \text{(multiply each product)} \\
&= 0.0786
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-exm-chance-agreement-prob-pos}

By the [complement rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#cor-p-neg0),
the probability of a negative test is:

$$
\ba
\Prf{\neg +}
&= 1 - \Prf{+}
&& \text{(complement rule)} \\
&= 1 - 0.0786
&& \text{(substitute } \Prf{+} \text{)} \\
&= 0.9214
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-exm-chance-agreement-prob-neg}

With $\Prf{D} = 0.07$ and $\Prf{\neg D} = 0.93$ (@exm-prevalence),
the [chance agreement](#def-chance-agreement) is:

$$
\ba
p_e
&= \Prf{+} \cd \Prf{D} + \Prf{\neg +} \cd \Prf{\neg D}
&& \text{(definition of } p_e \text{)} \\
&= 0.0786 \cd 0.07 + 0.9214 \cd 0.93
&& \text{(substitute the marginal probabilities)} \\
&= 0.005502 + 0.856902
&& \text{(multiply each product)} \\
&= 0.862404
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-exm-chance-agreement}

Because nearly everyone tests negative and does not have COVID-19,
two [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) classifiers with these marginal [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability)
would agree on about 86% of people by chance alone.

:::
